title: Complete an FAA Form 337 for a major repair or alteration
subject: General
assumptions: A written determination classifies the work as repair or alteration and as major or minor before the form is started.
The classification reached matches the actual work scope and correctly concludes Form 337 is required.
If a certificated repair station did the major repair, the work order plus signed maintenance release alternative is addressed.
The assembled data package qualifies as approved data (e.g., STC, TCDS, AD, DER-approved data, FAA-approved SB), not merely acceptable data.
If no previously approved data exists, a field approval package is initiated instead of proceeding on unapproved data.
Block 2 is filled in as part of the front-side entries completed through block 6 before submission.
openQuestions: Every check, error mode and evidence item in this pack was drafted by packs/compile_pack.py from the procedure sheet and handbook, and has not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.

Confirm the governing reference: the sheet names AC 43.9-1G, while FAA-H-8083-30B pp. 2-14 to 2-17 was located during compilation and is flagged assumed — an SME must decide which governs and whether the handbook attributions stand.
Confirm the 48-hour FAA submission window against the current AC 43.9-1G and 14 CFR 43.9 text, since it appears only in the campus sheet.
Specify the exercise inputs: is this a live aircraft, a scenario packet, or a bench article, and which data plate and registration record the student is expected to work from?

Rule on block 6 C/D for uncertificated students — whether a training signature or 'FOR TRAINING ONLY' annotation is required, and how that interacts with the 'sign only when work has been completed' note.
Decide whether the field-approval variant (block 3 left open) is a required condition for every submission or only for a designated scenario.

subtasks.label: Procedure
subtasks.excluded: 25 [document] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

checks.text: A written determination classifies the work as repair or alteration and as major or minor before the form is started.
checks.src: Handbook: "First consider whether this a repair or an alteration" and whether work "constitutes a major or a minor maintenance action"; assumed reference needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The determination cites 14 CFR part 43 appendix A (paragraph/example) as the basis for the 'major' classification.
checks.src: Procedure note 1: required when work meets the "major" requirement "outlined in 14 CFR part 43 appendix A".

checks.text: The classification reached matches the actual work scope and correctly concludes Form 337 is required.
checks.src: Handbook: "If the maintenance accomplished was a major repair or alteration, the work must be documented on FAA Form 337"; provisional, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: If a certificated repair station did the major repair, the work order plus signed maintenance release alternative is addressed.
checks.src: Handbook: signed work order "accompanied by a signed maintenance release may be used in lieu of the FAA Form 337"; uncited extract, SME confirmation needed.

errors.text: Work that is minor is classified as major (or vice versa), so the wrong record type is generated.
Determination made with no citation to 14 CFR part 43 appendix A or other authority.
Alteration described as a repair (or reverse) in the determination, mislabeling block 4 downstream.
Determination is illegible, undated, or unsigned scratch notes.

checks.text: The assembled data package qualifies as approved data (e.g., STC, TCDS, AD, DER-approved data, FAA-approved SB), not merely acceptable data.
checks.src: Handbook: "Major repairs and alterations require 'approved data.' Some examples of approved data are AD notes, STCs, TCDS, DER-specific delegations, and FAA-approved manufacturer Service Bulletins"; assumed reference needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: Each data item shows applicability/effectivity covering the specific aircraft make, model and serial number being worked.
checks.src: Sheet note 2 requires "applicable reference data to complete the work"; applicability is what makes data usable on this product.

checks.text: The document number, revision level and date of each data item are identified and current at time of use.
checks.src: Sheet note 8 requires stating "what approved data was used" in block 8, which requires unique identification of the data.

checks.text: If no previously approved data exists, a field approval package is initiated instead of proceeding on unapproved data.
checks.src: Handbook: "the technician may request that the FAA accomplish a 'Field Approval'"; provisional — handbook not cited by the sheet, needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Acceptable data (maintenance manual, AC 43.13-1) is collected and used as the basis for a major repair or alteration.
An STC or drawing is used with no evidence of applicability to that make, model and serial number.
A superseded revision of the data is used, or the revision/date is never recorded for citation in block 8.

checks.text: All Block 1 fields — make, model, serial number, and nationality/registration mark — are filled with no blanks.
checks.src: Step note requires make, model, serial number and registration number to be entered in block 1.

checks.text: Make, model and serial number entered match the aircraft data plate exactly, character for character.
checks.src: Step note: 'Use the information from the aircraft's data plate'; verification requires comparing form to the data plate.

checks.text: Nationality and registration mark agree with the aircraft's registration records.
checks.src: Registration number must trace to registration records, not to memory or the tail marking alone.

checks.text: Entries are legible, in permanent ink, inside field boundaries, with no erasures or uninitialed corrections.
checks.src: Form 337 is a permanent aircraft record; workmanship standard for an official document entry.

errors.text: Serial number copied from logbook, invoice or memory rather than the data plate, giving a wrong but plausible entry.
Model or serial number transposed into the wrong field, or registration mark entered without nationality letter.
One Block 1 field left blank or filled in pencil, with smudged or overwritten characters.

checks.text: Block 2 shows a complete owner entry — name plus street, city, state and ZIP — with no blank lines.
checks.src: Note 4 directs the owner's name and address be entered in block 2; completeness is visible on the finished form.

checks.text: The name and address in block 2 match the aircraft's current registration record exactly.
checks.src: Note 4: 'Find the aircraft's registration records for the owner's name and address' — verification requires the registration document.

checks.text: Block 2 names the registered owner, not the mechanic, repair facility or requesting customer.
checks.src: Note 7 assigns the performing person's information to block 7A/B, keeping block 2 for the owner alone.

checks.text: Block 2 is filled in as part of the front-side entries completed through block 6 before submission.
checks.src: Handbook: 'the technician completes the front side of Form 337 through block 6'. Assumed reference; needs subject-matter confirmation.

errors.text: Owner name/address taken from the work order, logbook or data plate instead of the registration record, giving a plausible but outdated owner.
Block 2 left blank or missing address elements such as city, state or ZIP.
Entry illegible, overwritten or crossed out rather than cleanly corrected.

checks.text: Exactly one of the two options in block 4 — Repair or Alteration — is marked, never both and never left blank.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 5: "Select the correct action performed, either repair or alteration."

checks.text: The option marked matches the classification of the work: alteration if the aircraft was changed from its previous state, repair if returned to it.
checks.src: Handbook: "a repair basically returns the aircraft to its previous or unaltered condition"; "An alteration... always changes or modifies the aircraft." Handbook uncited — needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The block 4 selection is consistent with the approved data cited and the block 8 description of work (e.g., STC install marked as alteration).
checks.src: Notes 2 and 8 require approved data and a clear description; the classification must agree with them.

checks.text: The mark is legible and unambiguous, placed inside the intended box, with no erasure, overwriting or correction fluid.
checks.src: Form must read unambiguously as a permanent aircraft record; workmanship expectation of the sheet.

errors.text: Work that modified the aircraft (e.g., STC avionics install) is marked as Repair, so the form looks complete but records the wrong configuration change.
Both boxes marked, or neither marked, leaving the type of action undetermined.
Check mark straddles both boxes or is obscured by erasure/correction fluid, making the entry hard to read.

checks.text: Block 5 shows make, model and serial number only on the row for the unit actually repaired or altered, other rows blank or N/A.
checks.src: Sheet note 6: "Fill in the product's information such as make, model, and serial number."

checks.text: The make, model and serial number entered match the product's data plate and registration/maintenance records exactly.
checks.src: Sheet notes 3 and 6 require unit identity taken from the product's own data plate/records, not from memory.

checks.text: Block 5 entries are legible, in permanent ink, with no erasures, overwrites or correction fluid.
checks.src: Documentation convention supporting the sheet's configuration-history purpose; not stated verbatim in either source — needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: If the form is being submitted for field approval, Block 5 is complete along with the rest of the front side through Block 6, Block 3 left open.
checks.src: Handbook: "completes the front side of Form 337 through block 6 (leaving block 3 open for later FAA approval)"; extract not cited by sheet, confirm with SME.

errors.text: Serial number transposed or copied from a different unit, so the form looks complete but records the wrong product.
Unit data entered on the wrong row (e.g. appliance data on the airframe line) or Block 5 left blank.
Entries in pencil, illegible, or corrected by overwriting.

checks.text: Block 6 A, B, C and D are all completed: name/address, kind-of-agency box marked, certificate number, and dated signature.
checks.src: Note 7: "Fill in A and B with the person's information who performed the work"; signature block must be dated and signed.

checks.text: The pre-printed conformity statement is intact, unaltered and not struck through or overwritten.
checks.src: Note 7 requires the student to "Verify the conformity statement" before signing.

checks.text: The kind of agency marked and the certificate number entered match the credential actually held by the signer.
checks.src: Handbook 2-16: a certificated repairman is "not authorized to approve that product for RTS"; requires checking the certificate itself.

checks.text: The signature date is on or after the date the described work was actually completed.
checks.src: Note 7: "Sign only when work has been completed" — settled only against work records/logbook dates.

checks.text: If the job is a field approval, block 6 is completed but block 3 is left blank for FAA entry.
checks.src: Handbook: "completes the front side of Form 337 through block 6 (leaving block 3 open for later FAA approval)"; assumed reference, needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Block 6 signed and dated before the repair or alteration was actually finished.
Kind of agency or certificate number entered does not match the signer's actual authority (e.g. repairman signing conformity).
Block 6 partially completed — address, certificate number or date omitted — or signature illegible.

checks.text: Block 8 contains a legible narrative stating what work was done and how it was accomplished, not just a part number or bare reference.
checks.src: Procedure sheet note 8: "Explain clearly what was done, how it was done."

checks.text: Block 8 includes an airworthiness statement for the repair or alteration performed.
checks.src: Procedure sheet note 8 requires "an airworthiness statement" within the block 8 description.

checks.text: The data cited in block 8 is approved data identified by title, number and revision, and it actually covers the work described.
checks.src: Handbook p.2-16: "the work must be documented on FAA Form 337 and requires supporting approved data"; assumed reference, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: If continuation sheets are used, block 8 states where they are and each attached sheet is identifiable to this aircraft and date.
checks.src: Procedure sheet note 8: "If more space is needed, note where those pages are." Verification requires the attached pages.

errors.text: Block 8 cites only acceptable data (maintenance manual, AC 43.13-1) instead of approved data, while the form looks complete.
Narrative is vague boilerplate ("repaired IAW manual") omitting method, materials or extent of work.
Continuation pages used but not referenced in block 8 or not identified to the aircraft, so the record is incomplete.

checks.text: Three complete collated sets of the form — original plus two copies, including any block 8 continuation pages — are present.
checks.src: Sheet requires original for aircraft records, copy to owner, copy to FAA; all three must be complete sets.

checks.text: The wet-signed original is the copy filed with the aircraft records, not a photocopy.
checks.src: "Keep the original form 337 with the aircraft records" — which copy went where is only settled from the records file.

checks.text: The FAA copy is transmitted within 48 hours of work completion, evidenced by dated transmittal against the completion date.
checks.src: 48-hour limit stated by the procedure sheet only; handbook extract gives no distribution timing.

checks.text: Student identifies that a repair station major repair may use a signed work order plus maintenance release in lieu of Form 337.
checks.src: "a signed copy of the completed customer work order accompanied by a signed maintenance release may be used in lieu of the FAA Form 337"; uncited reference, needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: FAA copy never sent, or sent after the 48-hour window, while the file looks complete.
Original mailed to the FAA and a photocopy left in the aircraft records.
Owner never given a copy, or the copy omits block 8 continuation sheets.

checks.text: A separate logbook entry exists for the work in addition to the completed Form 337.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "does not replace a logbook entry"; handbook p.2-16: "the work must be documented on FAA Form 337" alongside the 43.9 record entry.

checks.text: The entry explicitly cross-references the Form 337 for the major repair or alteration.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 10 requires a write-up "with reference to the form 337"; handbook does not state this.

checks.text: The entry shows a description of the work, the completion date, and a signature with certificate number and type.
checks.src: Handbook: "What—a description of the work performed... When—the date the work was completed... the signature, certificate number, and type of certificate"; uncited source, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The work and approved data described in the entry agree with Form 337 block 8 and the aircraft records.
checks.src: Requires comparing the entry against the completed 337 and approved data; cannot be judged from the entry alone.

errors.text: No logbook entry made because the Form 337 was treated as sufficient documentation.
Entry is unsigned or omits certificate number/type, so no valid approval for return to service exists.
Entry is vague or omits the Form 337 reference, breaking the link to the approved data.
